messages.subject: A couple of usage questions about the Data Viewer
messages.subject_clean: A couple of usage questions about the Data Viewer
messages.body_plain:
StatET is a Godsend and I use it all day long.
In particular, I use the Data Viewer constantly.

Every time the underlying values change after I run some R code, I have 
to manually close the DataViewer of that data.table and reopen it 
manually to see the updates contents.  (Occasionally it detects the 
change and prompts me to refresh or reload it, but usually not except 
for gigantic data.tables).

Is there any command or key sequence or whatever to force it to 
refresh?  I have looked in vain but could have missed something.

My second question is whether there is any way to change the default 
width of the columns or make them auto-adjust to the data?  Many of my 
columns have IDates in the format 2011-02-11, and the first thing I have 
to do after opening a table is manually drag to widen all of the date 
columns so that I can see the end of the dates.

These are minor things but I just wanted to be sure I was not missing 
any features.

THANKS!

messages.body_plain:
Hello Don,

normally pressing F5 prompts to refresh or reload the data viewer. I had recently the problem that a new R console was opened instead of refreshing the data viewer but I could solve that by setting the Scheme under Window/Preferences/General/Keys to default.

marco

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

While editing an .R file, every time I do a search for a string, it 
moves nicely to highlight the first occurrence in the file BUT ALSO, 
unwanted, expands the separate outline view to such a level of detail 
that I cannot see what function the string it found is in.  I want to go 
next,next,next skipping over locations in methods that I am not 
interested in.   But it keeps expanding the outline view.  I cannot see 
the forest for the trees.  My functions are very long.

Is there any way to suppress the unwanted automatic expansion in the 
outline view that occurs for every search hit?  I want it to just 
highlight the name of the function in the outline view (which is the way 
I had it before doing the search and the way it behaves if I navigate 
manually around the file by scrolling and clicking), not expand the 
detail within the function in the outline view, shoving the function 
name out of visibility.

Thank you.
